meta.name: History
meta.about: How the ecosystem got here, in five eras from 2007 to 2026. The Drupal and ELMS:LN years are drawn from Bryan Ollendyke's 2015 M.S. thesis, Information Altruism (kept in PRAW), where Penn State appears as CentralU, ELMS as YourNetwork and Bryan as Technologist Zero; the HAX years from PRAW's WORLDVIEW, WINS and talks. Each event points at the piece of HAX it became.

kindLabels.rel: era to event; event to what it became

history.desc: How the ecosystem got here. The Drupal and ELMS:LN years come from Bryan's 2015 thesis, where Penn State is CentralU, ELMS is YourNetwork and Bryan is Technologist Zero; the rest from PRAW.

e_drupal.desc: 2005 to 2012: a weekend Drupal course, a community of practice, and a learning platform built in the open at Penn State.

e_elmsln.desc: 2012 to 2016: the e-Learning Management System becomes a network of small Drupal apps; the thesis names what made it spread.

e_turn.desc: 2015 to 2019: a note card, a friend pointing at a standard, three weeks off to rewrite a career, and a standard that settled in 2019.

e_hax.desc: 2017 on: the editor, then HAXcms on PHP, Node.js, the CLI and the MCP.

e_teach.desc: 2019 on: IST 256 every semester, where class projects become HAX components.

h_hired.desc: Keith Bailey, the director who wrote pagination JavaScript himself, hires Bryan into online learning in the College of Arts and Architecture. Bryan begins contributing open source code the same year.

h_elms.desc: The e-Learning Management System, YourNetwork in the thesis, is conceived inside Transformational Learning Services in the College of Arts and Architecture: a learning platform built by the people who teach with it. The thesis's record of it starts July 18, 2007.

h_weekend.desc: Bryan's weekend Drupal course, the start of a Drupal community at Penn State that grew to more than 50 developers and 1,000 sites by 2015.

h_altruism.desc: Building and sharing Drupal work with other units freely, so each could grow its own capacity. Units that received it went on to hire and build; the pattern the thesis later names information altruism.

h_interviews.desc: Interviews across the units that adopted ELMS: what made it approachable, the pull of a community, independence and empowerment, and the 'many hats' small teams wear.

h_modules.desc: A Drupal core maintainer with hundreds of contributed modules. The plugin lessons from those years are why HAX waited so long on a plugin architecture.

h_elmsln.desc: ELMS is rebuilt as the ELMS Learning Network: many small Drupal distributions (courses, studio, blog, interact, discussion) wired together, deployed with Drush recipes.

h_whitepaper.desc: 'ELMSLN: A Disruptive Learning Technology.' ELMS for Drupal 6 had passed 780,000 downloads on 12,000 Drupal systems; ELMS:LN is in use at Penn State and UW-Madison.

h_thesis.desc: Bryan's M.S. thesis in IST, advised by Andrea Tapia: how donating effort, a community of practice and a technology built in the open let a grassroots system spread across a university. Written in first and third person as Technologist Zero.

h_sustaining.desc: 'ELMS Learning Network: An EdTech Platform for Sustaining Innovation,' with Michael Collins.

h_notecard.desc: HAX starts as a note card, a napkin idea: an editor where you talk to the screen, in the Kinect era.

h_standard.desc: Mike Potter points Bryan to the web component standard itself, not a component library. It is what made HAX possible.

h_rewrite.desc: Bryan takes three weeks off to rewrite his career on a standard that would not stabilize until 2019. HAX becomes a proof of concept; the first element ships; DrupalCon DC hears about it.

h_stable.desc: Web components stabilize across browsers: 198 elements, the first site, 29 contributors, HAX Camp.

h_haxcms.desc: The smallest possible backend to make HAX work, writing sites to disk as JSON Outline Schema and HTML. DrupalCon Nashville.

h_2020.desc: hax.psu.edu opens on HAXiam; 582 elements and the first 11 sites. Because HAX saves HTML and ships the tag definitions separately, every site made since about 2020 still works.

h_2023.desc: Bill Rose's course ontology gives HAX its instructional backbone, and student contributors from IST 256 and HAX Lab carry feature output to its highest levels from 2024 on.

h_node.desc: HAXcms on Node.js with the same OpenAPI contract, the CLI, PRAW and the Future Traveler, the MCP.

h_ist256.desc: Bryan teaches IST 256 every semester from fall 2019 to spring 2026. Class projects become HAX components and students become contributors.

tours.label: Where it came from
tours.message: From a weekend Drupal course to the Future Traveler, in five eras. Over time plays it year by year.

scenes.caption: The Drupal years: Keith hires Bryan, ELMS is conceived, a weekend course seeds a community.
Donating effort builds capacity everywhere it lands; the thesis calls this information altruism.
ELMS becomes ELMS:LN, a network of small apps.
A note card, a friend pointing at a standard, three weeks off.
HAXcms, then every site since 2020 still works, then the classroom becomes the pipeline, then Node.js and agents.
And the classroom becomes the pipeline.
